subtitle: How Pamheiba Bent Kingdom, Gods and Memory to His Will

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the royal coronation hall, half in shadow, half in temple light
panels.action: King Pamheiba Gharib Niwaz stands between a Meitei sacred hearth and a rising Vaishnavite temple tower, one hand on his sword, the other on a palm-leaf manuscript, as courtiers bow in a dim, smoky hall.

dialogue.text: In the 1700s, King Pamheiba Gharib Niwaz renamed Kangleipak as Manipur, bowed to Vaishnav gods, rode against Ava—and forced a kingdom to choose which past to remember.

i18n.hi: १७०० के दशक में राजा पम्हैबा ग़रीब निवाज़ ने कंग्लैपाक का नाम मणिपुर रखा, वैष्णव देवताओं को माना, आवा पर चढ़ बैठे—और राज्य को मजबूर किया कि कौन‑सा अतीत याद रखे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Pamheiba seated on the Kangla throne
panels.action: Pamheiba sits straight-backed on the Kangla throne, face stern yet curious, as brahmins from the west display icons of Vishnu and Krishna alongside Meitei sacred objects before him.

dialogue.text: When Pamheiba took the Kangla throne, Kangleipak already stood at a crossroads, its old Meitei rites meeting brahmins and Vaishnav stories from the plains.

i18n.hi: जब पम्हैबा ने कंगला का तख़्त लिया, कंग्लैपाक पहले ही मोड़ पर था—पुराने मीतै रीति, मैदानों से आए ब्राह्मण और वैष्णव कथाओं से टकरा रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot, side view of Pamheiba listening intently
panels.action: A Vaishnav teacher sits cross-legged, gesturing toward a painted scene of Krishna, while Pamheiba leans forward, fingers tight on the carved arm of his throne, the court watching for his reaction.

dialogue.text: The king listened as Vaishnav teachers spoke of one supreme lord, of bhakti, of new songs and new rules that promised order to a restless land.

i18n.hi: राजा ने सुना जब वैष्णव आचार्य एक सर्वोच्च भगवान, भक्ति, नए गीत और नियमों की बातें करते जो अशांत धरती को क़ायदा देने का दावा करते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on Pamheiba’s face as he is anointed
panels.action: Oil gleams on Pamheiba’s forehead as a brahmin priest touches his brow with a tilak, while attendants hold a conch and a Vaishnav icon near his shoulder.

dialogue.text: In time, Pamheiba took Vaishnav initiation and the name Gharib Niwaz, letting the new faith flow into the old throne like fresh water into an ancient channel.

i18n.hi: धीरे‑धीरे पम्हैबा ने वैष्णव दीक्षा ली, ग़रीब निवाज़ नाम पाया, और नई आस्था को ऐसे राजसिंहासन में बहने दिया जैसे प्राचीन धार में उतरता ताज़ा जल।

panels.shot: wide shot of royal courtyard with courtiers lined up
panels.action: In the palace courtyard, nobles and officers stand in lines as a herald beside Pamheiba unfurls a scroll, while temple builders and scribes wait with tools and manuscripts.

dialogue.text: The chronicle remembers what followed as royal command: court and nobility pressed to accept Vaishnav rites, old names remade, new food rules proclaimed.

i18n.hi: इतिहास आगे की बात को शाही फ़रमान के रूप में दर्ज करता है: दरबार और रईसों पर वैष्णव रीतें मानने का दबाव, पुराने नाम बदले, नए खान‑पान के नियम ऐलान हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Pamheiba addressing a line of courtiers
panels.action: Pamheiba stands with one hand raised, addressing courtiers who look uneasy, some clutching their sacred threads, others glancing toward the palace hearth in the background.

dialogue.speaker: king_pamheiba_gharib_niwaz
dialogue.text: The king’s faith is the kingdom’s path. Stand with me.

i18n.hi: राजा की आस्था ही राज्य की राह है। मेरे साथ खड़े हो।

panels.shot: wide shot of a hillside with new temple under construction
panels.action: On a hill above the valley, artisans raise wooden scaffolding around a new Vaishnav temple while Pamheiba, on horseback, watches builders hoist bells and idols into place.

dialogue.text: New temples rose in wood and brick, Vaishnav images glowed in oil light, and priests from afar found patronage at the Meitei king’s court.

i18n.hi: नए मंदिर लकड़ी‑ईंट से उठे, वैष्णव मूर्तियाँ तेल के दीयों में जगमगाईं, दूर‑दराज़ के पुजारी मीतै दरबार में सरंक्षण पाए।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of a Meitei household shrine
panels.action: In a dim Meitei household, elders sit by the Sanamahi hearth shrine as a royal officer at the doorway reads out an order, children watching, torn between the hearth and the distant sound of temple bells.

dialogue.text: Yet the court chronicle also tells of pressure, of old Sanamahi shrines disturbed, of house and clan rites strained under the weight of new royal favour.

i18n.hi: पर दरबारी इतिहास दबाव की भी बात करता है—पुराने सनामाही देवस्थल हिले, घर और कुल की रीतियाँ नए राजाश्रय के बोझ तले खिंच गईं।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of palace kitchen and courtyard
panels.action: Palace cooks pour meat from a pot into a pit under the watch of inspectors, while a decree tablet is held up and Pamheiba passes by, expression set, as cattle graze unharmed beyond the wall.

dialogue.text: Pamheiba’s orders reached the kitchen and market too: beef forbidden by law, diet reshaped to fit the new Vaishnav ethic.

i18n.hi: पम्हैबा के हुक्म रसोई और बाज़ार तक पहुँचे: गोमांस क़ानून से मना, पूरा भोजनचर बदलकर नई वैष्णव नीति में ढाला गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of scribes at low desks in a royal library
panels.action: Scribes sit cross-legged in the royal library, copying Vaishnav texts from Devanagari onto Meitei manuscripts, while a priest and Pamheiba review the work with solemn care.

dialogue.text: Translations flowed. Vaishnav tales and rules were rendered in the Meitei tongue, stitched into the kingdom’s stories through ink and song.

i18n.hi: अनुवादों की बाढ़ चली—वैष्णव कथा और नियम मीतै भाषा में ढाले गए, स्याही और गीत के सहारे राज्य की कहानियों में टाँके गए।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a stack of palm-leaf Puyas beside new manuscripts
panels.action: A stack of old palm-leaf Puyas rests beside fresh Vaishnav manuscripts on a mat, a shaft of light dividing them, as Pamheiba’s shadow falls across both piles.

dialogue.text: Later memory tells of a great burning of Puyas in this reign. But the surviving chronicles are silent, and many Puyas still endure in archives and homes.

i18n.hi: बाद की यादें इस राज में बड़े पुइया‑दहन की बात कहती हैं। पर बचे हुए इतिहास चुप हैं, और बहुत‑से पुइया आज भी अभिलेखों और घरों में टिके हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of two scholars debating over manuscripts
panels.action: Two later-era scholars sit amid shelves of manuscripts, one pointing to an empty space in the chronicle, the other holding a Puya, while a faint imagined scene of flames hovers behind them like a half-remembered dream.

dialogue.text: Modern historians weigh passion against paper, noting the coercive change, yet finding no firm record of a single, ordered libricide in 1729.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार जोश और दस्तावेज़ दोनों तौलते हैं—ज़ोर ज़बरन बदलाव मानते हैं, पर १७२९ में किसी एक सुनियोजित ग्रंथ‑दहन का पक्का सबूत नहीं पाते।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of Pamheiba reviewing cavalry on a plain
panels.action: Pamheiba rides along a line of armored Meitei cavalry, spears glinting, as banners snap in the wind and the eastern hills rise like a wall behind them.

dialogue.text: While gods and books were reordered at home, Pamheiba hardened his army. Horses were shod, spears balanced, eyes turned toward the Irrawaddy and Ava.

i18n.hi: जब घर के देवता और किताबें फिर से सज रहीं, पम्हैबा ने अपनी सेना कड़ी कर दी—घोड़ों को नाल लगे, भाले सँवरे, नज़रें इरावदी और आवा की ओर मुड़ गईं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of Manipuri cavalry moving through forest toward a river
panels.action: Columns of Manipuri horsemen thread through dense forest toward a wide river, their reflections rippling on the water as Pamheiba leads from the front, pointing toward the far bank.

dialogue.text: From the chronicles we hear of deep raids toward Burmese lands, Manipuri cavalry pushing through forest and river toward the Irrawaddy frontier.

i18n.hi: इतिहास में हमें गहरे धावों की खबर मिलती है—बर्मा की तरफ़ तक, मणिपुरी घुड़सवार जंगल‑नदियाँ चीरते इरावदी की सरहद तक धकेलते गए।

panels.shot: mid-wide of a burning frontier town seen from a distance
panels.action: Pamheiba and his captains sit their horses on a ridge as a distant frontier settlement smokes, people fleeing along the riverbank, the sky darkened with ash and birds.

dialogue.text: War left its mark on both sides of the hills. Burmese chronicles remember Manipuri incursions; Meitei records speak of glory and captives won far from the Imphal valley.

i18n.hi: जंग ने दोनों पार के पहाड़ों पर निशान छोड़े—बर्मी इतिहास मणिपुरी चढ़ाइयों को याद रखते हैं, मीतै लेख दूर इम्फ़ाल घाटी से जीती शान और बंदियों की बात करते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a royal council with map and envoys
panels.action: In council, Pamheiba stands before a painted map showing Kangla, Bishnupur, Cachar, Tripura and the Irrawaddy frontier, while envoys from the west and east listen, hands folded.

dialogue.text: The court watched the wider chessboard—Bishnupur’s plains, Cachar’s hills, Tripura’s forests, the Burmese kingdoms—each neighbour weighing this new, assertive Manipur.

i18n.hi: दरबार ने बड़ा शतरंज देखा—बिष्णुपुर के मैदान, कछार की पहाड़ियाँ, त्रिपुरा के जंगल, बर्मा के राज्य—हर पड़ोसी इस नए, दबंग मणिपुर को तौल रहा था।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of Kangla fort and the valley
panels.action: From the Kangla wall, Pamheiba looks over the Imphal valley where new temples rise among old sacred groves, households smoke with evening fires, and distant riders follow a dusty road.

dialogue.text: In this mix of conquest and devotion, Pamheiba did more than rule. He tried to redraw the sacred map of his land.

i18n.hi: इस मिलावट में, जीत और भक्ति के बीच, पम्हैबा ने सिर्फ राज नहीं किया—वह अपनी धरती का पवित्र नक्शा ही बदलना चाहता था।

panels.shot: low-angle shot as Pamheiba proclaims the new name
panels.action: Before assembled courtiers and priests, Pamheiba raises his hand decisively as a court scribe steps forward with a fresh decree scroll, the word 'Manipur' implied in their solemn faces.

dialogue.text: It was in this reign that Kangleipak took a new name in the records—Manipur—its identity braided tighter to Sanskritic worlds even as older ties endured in homes and hills.

i18n.hi: इसी राज में कंग्लैपाक ने रिकॉर्डों में नया नाम लिया—मणिपुर—पहचान और कसकर संस्कृत जगत से बँधी, जबकि पुरानी डोर घरों और पहाड़ों में अभी भी चलती रही।

panels.shot: close-up on an elder’s hands touching both Puya and Vaishnav text
panels.action: In a later generation, an elder’s hands rest on an old Puya and a Vaishnav manuscript side by side, while children in the background watch a dance that blends traditional and Vaishnav forms.

dialogue.text: Centuries on, Manipur still carries both traces: Sanamahi hearth and Vaishnav temple, horse-war songs and bhakti dance, all shadowed by Pamheiba’s choice to use royal power to shape belief.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद भी मणिपुर दोनों निशान ढोता है—सनामाही की आँच और वैष्णव मंदिर, घोड़ा‑युद्ध के गीत और भक्ति का नाच—सब पर पम्हैबा के उस फ़ैसले की परछाईं, कि राजसत्ता से विश्वास को मोड़ सके।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Manipur’s landscape, valley to hills to distant rivers
panels.action: A sweeping view pulls back from the Imphal valley across temples, hearth-smoke, rivers and distant hills toward the east and west, the land quiet under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: Pamheiba changed laws, gods, even the kingdom’s name, but the record endures as a mirror, asking each age how far a ruler’s will may reach into the soul of a people.

i18n.hi: पम्हैबा ने क़ानून बदले, देवता बदले, राज्य का नाम तक बदला—पर इतिहास आज भी आईना है, जो हर दौर से पूछता है: शासक की मर्ज़ी जनता की आत्मा तक कितनी दूर जा सकती है?

subtitle_i18n.en: How Pamheiba Bent Kingdom, Gods and Memory to His Will
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे पम्हैबा ने राज्य, देवता और यादें अपनी मर्ज़ी से मोड़ीं
